records.useCase: A Reddit discussion discovered through the permitted paths (search snippets, notifications, manual submission): plain HTTP is blocked by the platform's anti-abuse controls and must stay unavailable rather than trigger circumvention.
records.groundingNote: Issue #17 recorded the permitted Reddit discovery paths: search-snippet discovery and manual submissions with snippet-level provenance, with post-ID identity merging search results, notification emails and submissions into one canonical item. The blocked body stays unavailable with its snippet provenance; Reddit access is never recovered by browser rendering.
records.permittedBasis: Reddit serves the discussion behind an anti-abuse control wall that blocks plain HTTP retrieval; retrieving the blocked body through a browser would circumvent a platform/anti-abuse restriction, which AGENTS.md and D11 prohibit regardless of technical reachability.

browser.reason: Refused: the blocked response is the platform's anti-abuse control. Rendering the blocked page in a browser would circumvent a platform restriction, so no render is measured, recorded or attempted; the discussion stays unavailable with its snippet-level provenance, exactly as issue #24's acceptance criteria require.

records.useCase: A permitted-origin page that gates readers behind a human-verification challenge: the shipped HTTP extractor already records it as an interstitial, and no browser render may resolve or bypass the challenge.
records.groundingNote: Interstitial anti-abuse controls are common where operators do not want automated reading; the shipped extractor already records these pages unavailable rather than attempting a bypass. Recorded to pin the boundary: a browser render that resolves or dodges the challenge is circumvention and stays unrecoverable.

newTrustBoundariesAdoptionWouldCreate: a long-lived networked browser/rendering subprocess executing untrusted page scripts inside the single-user monolith, with its own sandbox profile, binary installation and CVE maintenance cadence
a budget ledger for per-render timeout/memory, concurrency and daily render counts that core HTTP ingestion does not need
a second provenance surface (browser-rendered text) that must stay honestly separated from http-method extraction and record its simulated/real sandboxed method

liveMeasurement.note: This replay launches no browser and fetches nothing: both arms are recorded/simulated, and the recorded decision rests on the deterministic replay plus the documented terms/cost analysis. A bounded live capability probe (agent-browser CLI against a localhost-only page; no external egress; no third-party or Reddit navigation) was performed out-of-band while recording this evaluation; its environment-specific observations are documented in docs/evaluation.md and deliberately excluded from this byte-reproducible baseline.

adoption.threshold: Adopt a minimal optional browser-extraction adapter only when the recorded corpus contains at least one use case that satisfies ALL of: (a) observed limitation — the use case is grounded in recorded deployment evidence (an unavailable extraction result, or a submitted URL whose content the shipped HTTP-only extractor could not obtain), not a synthetic capability probe; (b) permitted render — the page is readable without authentication, without a robots/terms prohibition and without defeating a platform or anti-abuse control, so a browser render circumvents nothing (a blocked Reddit response never qualifies regardless of technical reachability and stays unavailable); (c) affordable — the render fits the explicit per-render timeout and memory budgets, the concurrency budget and the daily render budget while the adapter stays sandboxed, secret-free and provenance-preserving; and (d) lift — the browser-equivalent text materially exceeds what the HTTP-only baseline recorded, recovering content the pipeline demonstrably lacks. Otherwise record a justified non-adoption with the per-record rejection reasons.
